zh.headline: 卡拉什尼科夫 AK-47 第三型突击步枪：1949 年机械传奇与工程剖析
zh.deck: 米哈伊尔·卡拉什尼科夫设计的 AK-47 第三型采用整块锻钢铣削机匣与超大间隙长行程导气活塞，配合宽大双闭锁突笋与锥形弹壳抽壳几何，在泥沙、严寒与长期免维护条件下确立了人类轻武器可靠性的工业基准。 本馆以 1:1 真实工程比例重现其 20 大核心构件与完整工作循环。

acts.title: 时代召唤与研发立项：AK-47 Type 3 的诞生背景
paragraphs: 1949 年问世的 卡拉什尼科夫 AK-47 第三型突击步枪 由苏联伊热夫斯克机械制造厂（Izhmash）主导研制，定位为经典的突击步枪。1949 年苏军正式列装 AK-47，1955 年定型的第三型铣削机匣版本凭借卓越工艺成为世界各国步枪仿制与现代改进的母本，衍生族谱产量突破一亿支。
米哈伊尔·卡拉什尼科夫设计的 AK-47 第三型采用整块锻钢铣削机匣与超大间隙长行程导气活塞，配合宽大双闭锁突笋与锥形弹壳抽壳几何，在泥沙、严寒与长期免维护条件下确立了人类轻武器可靠性的工业基准。 整件装备总长 880 mm（固定桦木层压枪托）、空重 3.8 kg，成为同期突击步枪领域最具辨识度的里程碑之一。
acts.audioScript: 第一幕，时代起源。1949 年，苏联伊热夫斯克机械制造厂（Izhmash）推出了划时代的卡拉什尼科夫 AK-47 第三型突击步枪。1949 年苏军正式列装 AK-47，1955 年定型的第三型铣削机匣版本凭借卓越工艺成为世界各国步枪仿制与现代改进的母本，衍生族谱产量突破一亿支。 它的核心设计聚焦于与枪机框一体连结的长行程重型活塞，提供充沛过驱动抽壳能量，奠定了其在突击步枪发展史中的经典地位。
acts.focusPartLabel: 主体机匣与闭锁承力框架

acts.title: 核心机械构造与闭锁奥秘
paragraphs: 卡拉什尼科夫 AK-47 第三型突击步枪 的机械灵魂在于其「长行程导气活塞 · 双闭锁突笋 35° 回转枪机与整锻铣削机匣」结构体系。在发射工作循环中，长行程导气活塞带动枪机框完成自由行程并驱动旋转闭锁解锁，将高压能量精确约束于承力框架之内。
制造工艺方面，关键承力件采用苏联烤漆冲压钢与酚醛玻璃纤维电木精加工而成。整锻铣削机匣配合双侧减重槽，消除早期冲压工艺刚度不足问题，在严苛实战条件下依然保持顺畅节拍与长期尺寸稳定性。
acts.audioScript: 第二幕，核心机械原理。卡拉什尼科夫 AK-47 第三型突击步枪 采用长行程导气活塞 · 双闭锁突笋 35° 回转枪机与整锻铣削机匣。在每个击发周期中，长行程导气活塞带动枪机框完成自由行程并驱动旋转闭锁解锁。借助苏联烤漆冲压钢与酚醛玻璃纤维电木工艺与高强度配合，实现了整锻铣削机匣配合双侧减重槽，消除早期冲压工艺刚度不足问题。
acts.focusPartLabel: 高强度闭锁枪机头与抽壳钩

acts.title: 弹道性能、内膛工艺与实战效能
paragraphs: 该平台配用 7.62×39mm M43 弹药规格与 415 mm 镀铬冷锻枪管（4 条右旋膛线 · 240 mm 缠距），最高工作膛压约 355 MPa，可赋予弹头 715 m/s 的出膛初速与 2,010 J 动能，有效作用距离达 350 米。
内膛技术特点方面，4 条硬铬内膛切削膛线与锥度弹膛，兼顾极寒与风沙抽壳可靠性。同时，大锥度 7.62×39mm M43 弹膛与刚性抓壳钩实现强力一次预抽壳，令其在 600 发/分（自动）· 40–100 发/分（战斗） 的节奏下兼具精准控制与可靠输出。
acts.audioScript: 第三幕，弹道与实战表现。配备 415 毫米身管与 7.62×39mm M43 口径，卡拉什尼科夫 AK-47 第三型突击步枪 实现了每秒 715 米的初速与 350 米有效射程。4 条硬铬内膛切削膛线与锥度弹膛，兼顾极寒与风沙抽壳可靠性，展现了卓越的工程平衡。

acts.title: 人机工效、供弹哲学与百年遗产
paragraphs: 围绕 30 发容量的30 发可拆式双排弹匣壳体与 44 mm 膛轴设计，卡拉什尼科夫 AK-47 第三型突击步枪 将单发后坐冲量控制在 7.8 N·s 水平。标志性右侧大片防尘快慢机兼任保险与机匣抛壳窗防尘盖。
如今在数字兵器库 3D 百年展厅（BAY-35）中，您可以随时通过三轴剖视、100% 爆炸视图与实时运动学滑块，零距离拆解这座跨越时代的机械工程杰作。

acts.title: Origins & Operational Mandate of the AK-47 Type 3
paragraphs: Introduced in 1949 by Izhmash Arsenal in Soviet Union, the Kalashnikov AK-47 Type 3 emerged as a defining Assault Rifle. Adopted by the Soviet Army in 1949 and refined into the definitive milled Type 3 in 1955, the AK-47 became the most widely produced infantry rifle lineage in history with over 100 million derivatives.

Mikhail Kalashnikov’s Type 3 AK-47 pairs a forged, milled-steel receiver with a generous-clearance long-stroke gas piston and dual-lug rotating bolt, setting the global industrial benchmark for mud, ice, and sand reliability. Measuring 880 mm (Fixed Laminated Wood Stock) at an unloaded weight of 3.8 kg, it reshaped expectations across the Assault & Battle Rifle class.
acts.audioScript: Act One: Historical Origins. In 1949, Izhmash Arsenal of Soviet Union introduced the Kalashnikov AK-47 Type 3. Adopted by the Soviet Army in 1949 and refined into the definitive milled Type 3 in 1955, the AK-47 became the most widely produced infantry rifle lineage in history with over 100 million derivatives. Anchored by its hallmark design trait — One-piece long-stroke piston and heavy bolt carrier deliver high over-gassed extraction authority — it quickly established an enduring engineering benchmark.

acts.title: Core Operating Architecture & Lockup Mechanics
paragraphs: At the mechanical heart of the Kalashnikov AK-47 Type 3 sits its Long-Stroke Gas Piston · Dual-Lug 35° Rotating Bolt in Forged Milled Receiver. Throughout every firing cycle, long-stroke gas piston drives carrier free-travel before cam-rotating the locking bolt, containing 355 MPa of operating pressure safely.

Constructed in Soviet-enamel stamped steel and glass-filled Bakelite, the assembly achieves durable field tolerances. Notably, Forged milled receiver with lightening cuts solves early stamped-sheet rigidity tolerances, sustaining dependable operation under severe environmental stress.
acts.audioScript: Act Two: Core Mechanical Architecture. The Kalashnikov AK-47 Type 3 relies on Long-Stroke Gas Piston · Dual-Lug 35° Rotating Bolt in Forged Milled Receiver. During each cycle, long-stroke gas piston drives carrier free-travel before cam-rotating the locking bolt. Machined from Soviet-enamel stamped steel and glass-filled Bakelite, it delivers standout engineering reliability: Forged milled receiver with lightening cuts solves early stamped-sheet rigidity tolerances.

acts.title: Ballistic Performance, Bore Craft & Range Reach
paragraphs: Chambered for 7.62×39mm M43 with 415 mm Chrome-Lined Barrel (4-Groove RH · 1:9.45" / 240 mm Twist), the Kalashnikov AK-47 Type 3 develops 715 m/s muzzle velocity and 2,010 J of kinetic energy for effective engagement out to 350 meters.

Internally, 4-groove hard-chrome bore paired with tapered 7.62×39mm chamber geometry for harsh-environment extraction. Combined with its 600 RPM cyclic · 40–100 RPM practical tempo, Generously tapered 7.62×39mm chamber and robust claw extractor ensure positive primary extraction, delivering disciplined accuracy across demanding field conditions.
acts.audioScript: Act Three: Ballistic Performance. Driving 7.62×39mm M43 through its 415 millimeter bore, the Kalashnikov AK-47 Type 3 achieves 715 meters per second and 350 meters of effective reach. 4-groove hard-chrome bore paired with tapered 7.62×39mm chamber geometry for harsh-environment extraction.

paragraphs: Fed by a 30-round 30-round detachable magazine body with a 44 mm bore-axis height, the platform manages 7.8 N-s of recoil impulse cleanly. Iconic right-side dust-cover selector lever doubles as ejection-port seal and fire control.
Now archived in Digital Armory 3D Centennial Gallery (BAY-35), all 20 interactive assemblies can be sectioned live along three axes, exploded to 100%, and inspected part by part.
